newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady at 3.07 to 3.09 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady at 3.07 to 3.09 pct.

text.p: German call rates were little changed from Friday at around 3.07 to 3.09 percent but underlying demand remained strong after last month's scramble for funds, traders said on Monday.
Some banks were nervous about being left short of funds this month after June when many had to resort to heavy borrowing at the costly Lombard window to meet monthly reserve targets, dealers said.
Some, however, said such worries are unfounded as the month was still young and there was ample time to trim positions if credit institutions feel liquidity is tight.
Banks held 39.8 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Friday, leaving the average for the month so far at 41.3 billion marks.
Banks borrowed only 100 million marks from the Lombard window.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA stood at 3,10467 percent on Monday compared with 3,10267 percent on Friday.
